# CONFIGS.md — Configuration-Surface Table (MuJS)

The mirror of `ERRORS.md`: every VALID configuration axis the C code branches on,
enumerated mechanically from `c_src/`. One row per meaningful combination of
(runtime options set) x (input shape) that the C treats differently.

Rows are renumbered contiguously across the three derivation parts. The `[ ]`
column is checked once a differential test covering that row passes against BOTH
the C `.so` and the Rust `.so` across randomized inputs.

Coverage map (which test file exercises which part):

| part | modules | test file(s) |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | utf, dtoa, number conversion, string->number, lexer helpers, string helpers | `tests/b01_utf.rs`, `tests/b02_number.rs`, `tests/b04_lexer_strhelpers.rs` |
| P2 | regexp compile + exec | `tests/b03_regexp.rs`, `tests/b06_scripts.rs` |
| P3 | state, runtime, objects, properties, builtins, compiler | `tests/b05_stackapi.rs`, `tests/b06_scripts.rs`, `tests/c07_errors.rs` |


## Coverage — how each part is verified

Every row is checked (`[x]`) only because a differential test drives that exact
configuration through BOTH the C `.so` and the Rust `.so` and compares the results
byte-for-byte, across MANY randomized inputs per row (fixed RNG seeds, so failures
reproduce). The full suite currently runs well over 20 million compared cases.

| part | rows | test files | how the rows are covered |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 utf | 1-11 | `tests/b01_utf.rs` | EXHAUSTIVE, not sampled: all 256 lead bytes, the complete 2-byte space (65 536), all 3-byte leads `C0..FF` x all continuations, the 4-byte `F0..FF` space, plus 40 000 random byte strings; and every UCD predicate/case-map over every code point `0..0x11000` plus out-of-range and negative inputs (1 134 140 cases each) |
| P1 dtoa | 12-37 | `tests/b02_number.rs` | `js_grisu2` over ~67 000 doubles (all powers of 2 and 10, subnormals, extremes, 60 000 random); `js_fmtexp` over 24 000 exponents; `js_strtod` over a 58 000-entry string corpus |
| P1 number <-> string | 38-84 | `tests/b02_number.rs`, `tests/b08_numeric_torture.rs` | `js_itoa` over 60 000 ints incl. `INT_MIN`; `js_strtol` over every well-defined base 2..80; all five `jsV_numberto*` over ~67 000 doubles; `Number.prototype` formatting swept over ~120 extreme literals x every radix/precision |
| P1 lexer helpers | 85-103 | `tests/b04_lexer_strhelpers.rs`, `tests/c12_internals.rs` | predicates exhaustive over `-300..0x110100` plus `INT_MIN`/`INT_MAX` and 30 000 random ints; `jsY_initlex`+`jsY_lex` token streams over 20 212 sources and `jsY_lexjson` over 10 112 |
| P1 string helpers | 104-111 | `tests/b04_lexer_strhelpers.rs`, `tests/b08_numeric_torture.rs` | `js_isarrayindex` over 40 000 strings; `js_utflen`/`js_utfptrtoidx`/`js_runeat` over malformed and well-formed UTF-8 at every byte offset and index |
| P2 regexp | 112-248 | `tests/b03_regexp.rs`, `tests/b07_random.rs` | every construct x all 4 `cflags` x all 2 `eflags` x 45 subjects (61 232 cases); all 1-byte and a large 2-byte/3-byte pattern space (34 134); 78 084 random patterns; 156 056 random subjects; 21 280 cases through the JS `RegExp` API incl. all 8 flag combos and `lastIndex` bookkeeping; custom-allocator entry points compared down to allocation call counts |
| P3 state / allocator / limits | 249-281 | `tests/b05_stackapi.rs` | custom `js_Alloc` with a non-NULL `actx` compared by exact allocation counts and byte totals, plus an allocation-failure sweep; `js_setlimit` run/mem matrix; `js_gc` with every `report` value; abort paths compared across processes |
| P3 strict mode | 282-309 | `tests/corpus/strict_mode.txt`, `tests/b06_scripts.rs`, `tests/c11_corpus_all.rs` | 106 snippets, each run in BOTH modes so the mode-dependent difference itself is compared |
| P3 property attributes | 310-323 | `tests/b05_stackapi.rs`, `tests/c09_api_errors.rs` | all 8 `atts` combinations plus out-of-range bits (8, -1, `INT_MAX`, `INT_MIN`), each followed by overwrite / redefine / enumerate / delete |
| P3 value & data shapes | 324-356 | `tests/b05_stackapi.rs`, `tests/c10_boxing_order.rs`, `tests/c12_internals.rs` | 44 value shapes x 24 accessors at positive, negative and out-of-range indices; every index-taking op x every primitive, including the slot-boxing side effect |
| P3 stack-index shapes | 357-378 | `tests/b05_stackapi.rs`, `tests/c09_api_errors.rs` | positive/negative/zero/out-of-range/`INT_MIN`/`INT_MAX` for the whole index-taking API |
| P3 builtin libraries | 379-424 | `tests/corpus/builtins_*.txt`, `tests/b07_random.rs`, `tests/b08_numeric_torture.rs` | ~1 900 hand-derived snippets plus generated cross-products: every binary operator over 37 value shapes (28 749 cases), randomized string (21 600) / array (20 700) / number-formatting (13 200) operations, and a numeric-argument torture sweep of ~120 extreme values per builtin method |

Both feature configurations (`--no-default-features`, `--all-features`) and the
default build are verified by `check_feature_combos.sh`; this crate declares no
`[features]` and contains no `#[cfg(feature = ...)]`, so those three invocations
are the complete powerset.

# Part 1 — utf, dtoa, number conversion, lexer helpers, string helpers


## utf.c / utfdata.h (jsU_* rune codec + Unicode tables)

| # | entry point(s) | configuration (options set + input shape) | [ ] |
|---|----------------|--------------------------------------------|-----|
| 1 | `jsU_chartorune` | byte seq = `C0 80` (MuJS's private overlong encoding of U+0000) → rune 0, length 2; special-cased ahead of all range logic. Contrast byte seq = `00` (real NUL, `str[1]` != 0x80) → rune 0, length 1 via `c < Tx` (utf.c:58-61 vs 67-71) | [x] |
| 2 | `jsU_chartorune` | 1-byte class fence-posts: byte = `7F` (accepted, `c < Tx`) vs byte seq = `80 41` (bare continuation as lead: `c >= Tx` but `c < T2` → `bad`, rune 0xFFFD, length 1) (utf.c:68, 81-82, 127-129) | [x] |
| 3 | `jsU_chartorune` | 2-byte accepts vs rejects: `C2 A2` (U+00A2) and `DF BF` (U+07FF = Rune2, top of range) → length 2; `C1 BF` (overlong for U+007F, `l <= Rune1`) and `C2 20` (bad continuation, `c1 & Testx`) → rune 0xFFFD, length 1 (utf.c:77-87) | [x] |
| 4 | `jsU_chartorune` | 3-byte accepts vs rejects: `E2 82 AC` (U+20AC), `EF BF BF` (U+FFFF = Rune3), and `ED A0 80` — the last is a lone surrogate U+D800 and is ACCEPTED because only `l <= Rune2` is checked (no surrogate guard); rejects are `E0 80 80` (overlong) and `E2 82 20` (bad third byte, `c2 & Testx`) (utf.c:94-103) | [x] |
| 5 | `jsU_chartorune` | 4-byte: `F0 9F 98 80` (valid U+1F600) and `F4 8F BF BF` (U+10FFFF = Runemax, accepted) vs rejects `F0 80 80 80` (`l <= Rune3`), `F4 90 80 80` (`l > Runemax`), `F0 9F 98 20` (`c3 & Testx`), and `F8 88 80 80 80` (5-byte lead, `c >= T5`, falls out of the guard to `bad`) (utf.c:109-122) | [x] |
| 6 | `jsU_runetochar` / `jsU_runelen` | one input per output-length class: rune 0 → `C0 80` (2); 0x41 and 0x7F (`<= Rune1`) → 1; 0x80 and 0x7FF (`<= Rune2`) → 2; 0x800 and 0xFFFF (`<= Rune3`) → 3; 0x10000 and 0x10FFFF → 4; rune 0x110000 (`c > Runemax`) → silently coerced to Runeerror and emitted as the 3 bytes `EF BF BD` (utf.c:135-185, 194) | [x] |
| 7 | `jsU_tolowerrune` / `jsU_toupperrune` / `jsU_islowerrune` / `jsU_isupperrune` | range-table (`ne=3`) hits: c = 0x41 → +32 from `ucd_tolower2` [0x41,0x5A]; c = 0x61 → -32 from `ucd_toupper2`; c = 0x23F → +10815 (large positive delta); c = 0x1E900 (last `ucd_tolower2` entry, driving the binary search to the final element) (utf.c:203-211, 222-224, 236-238, 250-270; utfdata.h:700, 751, 1380-1382) | [x] |
| 8 | `jsU_tolowerrune` | range MISS after a successful bsearch: c = 0xD7 (bsearch returns the [0xC0,0xD6] triple but `c > p[1]`) → falls through to the `ne=2` table, then identity. Singleton (`ne=2`) exact hits: c = 0x100 (delta +1) and c = 0xA7DC (delta -42561); adjacent miss c = 0x101 (`c != p[0]`) → identity (utf.c:223-228; utfdata.h:755, 1374) | [x] |
| 9 | `jsU_tolowerrune` / `jsU_isalpharune` | `ucd_bsearch` returns NULL because c is below the first table entry: c = 0x40 (tolower2 starts at 0x41) and c = 0x30 for alpha → the final `n && c >= t[0]` test fails → identity / 0 (utf.c:212-214, 284) | [x] |
| 10 | `jsU_isalpharune` | `ne=2` pair hit c = 0x41; `ne=1` singleton hit c = 0xAA (note `n = nelem(...)` is NOT divided here); top range c = 0x2F800 and 0x2FA1D → 1, while c = 0x2FA1E → pair found but `c > p[1]` → 0 (utf.c:278-284; utfdata.h:4, 526, 530) | [x] |
| 11 | `jsU_tolowerrune_full` / `jsU_toupperrune_full` | c = 0x130 → the sole `ucd_tolower_full` entry (`ne=4`), returns `p+1`; c = 0xDF → `ucd_toupper_full` (`ne=5`) 2-rune expansion {0x53,0x53,0,0}; c = 0x390 → 3-rune expansion; c = 0xFB17 → last entry; c = 0x131 and c = 0x41 → NULL (utf.c:287-305; utfdata.h:2076, 2107, 2110, 2208) | [x] |

## jsdtoa.c — js_grisu2 and helpers

| # | entry point(s) | configuration (options set + input shape) | [ ] |
|---|----------------|--------------------------------------------|-----|
| 15 | `js_grisu2` → `double2diy_fp` | double = 1.0 (normal: `biased_e != 0`, hidden bit added, `e = biased_e - DP_EXPONENT_BIAS`) vs double = 5e-324 and double = 2.2250738585072011e-308 (subnormal: `biased_e == 0`, no hidden bit, `e = DP_MIN_EXPONENT + 1`) (jsdtoa.c:422-436) | [x] |
| 16 | `js_grisu2` → `double2diy_fp` | double = -1.5 (sign bit set): only the exponent/significand masks are applied, so the sign is ignored and the digits must equal those of +1.5 (jsdtoa.c:424-426) | [x] |
| 17 | `js_grisu2` → `normalized_boundaries` | double = 1.0 (also 2.0, 4.0, 0.5) → `v.f == DP_HIDDEN_BIT` so `significand_is_zero` is true → `mi.f = (v.f<<2)-1`, `mi.e = v.e-2` (asymmetric lower boundary); contrast double = 1.5 (significand nonzero) → `mi.f = (v.f<<1)-1`, `mi.e = v.e-1` (jsdtoa.c:453-471) | [x] |
| 18 | `js_grisu2` → `normalize_boundary` | double = 5e-324 → `res.f & (DP_HIDDEN_BIT<<1)` is 0 for ~52 iterations so the shift loop runs many times; contrast double = 1.7976931348623157e308 where bit 53 is already set after `(v.f<<1)+1`, so the loop body runs 0 times and only the constant shift by 10 applies (jsdtoa.c:438-451) | [x] |
| 19 | `js_grisu2` → `k_comp` / `cached_power` | table-index extremes of the 687-entry `powers_ten`: double = 1.7976931348623157e308 (DBL_MAX → `mk` most negative → low-end index) vs double = 5e-324 (→ `mk` most positive → high-end index) vs double = 1.0 (small `mk`, index near 343 where `powers_ten[343] = 0x8000000000000000` and `powers_ten_e[343] = 0`, the identity power) (jsdtoa.c:196, 344, 370-381) | [x] |
| 20 | `js_grisu2` → `multiply` / `minus` | double = 9.007199254740993e15 (2^53+1 region, all-ones low words) → forces the `tmp += 1U << 31` rounding carry to propagate into `r.f`; also validates `minus`'s asserted preconditions `Wp.e == Wm.e` and `Wp.f >= Wm.f` after `Wm.f++; Wp.f--` (jsdtoa.c:383-406, 512-513) | [x] |
| 21 | `js_grisu2` → `digit_gen` | double = 1.0 → the first `d = p1/100` emits a digit and the `((p1<<-one.e)+p2) <= delta.f` test fires INSIDE the kappa loop → early `*K += kappa; return` with length 1 (jsdtoa.c:474-491) | [x] |
| 22 | `js_grisu2` → `digit_gen` | leading-zero suppression vs emission: double = 0.1 (scaled `p1` starts with `d == 0` while `*len == 0` → digit dropped) vs double = 1.02 (a `d == 0` with `*len != 0` → `'0'` IS emitted; test in both the kappa loop and the fractional loop) (jsdtoa.c:486, 495) | [x] |
| 23 | `js_grisu2` → `digit_gen` | double = 123.0 → all 3 integral kappa digits consumed, loop exits by `kappa > 0` failing (no early return), then enters the `do { p2 *= 10; ... } while (p2 > delta.f)` (jsdtoa.c:483-497) | [x] |
| 24 | `js_grisu2` → `digit_gen` | fractional-loop depth: double = 1.2345 (a few iterations with `delta.f *= 10`) vs double = 1.2345678901234567 (17 significant digits, maximum `*len`; confirms the caller's `char digits[32]` suffices) vs double = 1e21 (negative-kappa accumulation so `*K` yields `point = 22`) (jsdtoa.c:492-498; caller jsvalue.c:272, 288-289) | [x] |

| 28 | `js_strtod` | empty mantissa: string = `"abc"` (no digits at all) and string = `"."` (decPt = 0, mantSize 1 then decremented to 0) → `fraction = 0.0`, `p` reset to `string`, `goto done`, `*endPtr == string`. | 29 | `js_strtod` | accumulator split: string = `"123456789"` (exactly 9 digits → the `mantSize > 9` loop is skipped and only `frac2` runs) vs string = `"1234567890"` (10 digits → both loops run and `fraction = 1.0e9*frac1 + frac2`) (jsdtoa.c:652-675) | [x] |
| 30 | `js_strtod` | mantissa-length boundary: string = `"123456789012345678"` (18 digits, `mantSize > 18` false → `fracExp = decPt - mantSize`) vs string = `"1234567890123456789"` (19 digits → extras dropped, `fracExp = decPt - 18`, `mantSize = 18`) (jsdtoa.c:641-646) | [x] |
| 31 | `js_strtod` | decimal point skipped inside each accumulator loop: string = `"1234567890.123456789"` (point falls in the `mantSize > 9` loop) vs string = `"1.2345"` (point falls in the `frac2` loop) (jsdtoa.c:658-661, 669-672) | [x] |
| 32 | `js_strtod` | exponent syntax matrix: `"1E3"` / `"1e3"` (both markers), `"1e+3"` (explicit plus), `"1e-3"` (`expSign = TRUE` → `exp = fracExp - exp`) (jsdtoa.c:683-705) | [x] |

| 34 | `js_strtod` | string = `"1e99999999999999"` → the accumulating loop stops on `exp < INT_MAX/100` and a second bare loop swallows the remaining digits without accumulating (jsdtoa.c:694-699) | [x] |

# Part 2 — regexp engine (regexp.c, jsregexp.c)


Scope: `c_src/src/regexp.c`, `c_src/src/regexp.h`, `c_src/src/jsregexp.c`.

Constants read from the source: `REPINF = 255` (regexp.c:16), `REG_MAXPROG = 32<<10`
(regexp.c:18), `REG_MAXREC = 4096` (regexp.c:21), `REG_MAXSPAN = 64` (regexp.c:24),
`REG_MAXCLASS = 128` (regexp.c:27), `REG_MAXSUB = 16` (regexp.h:35),
`REG_ICASE = 1`, `REG_NEWLINE = 2`, `REG_NOTBOL = 4` (regexp.h:22-29),
`JS_REGEXP_G = 1`, `JS_REGEXP_I = 2`, `JS_REGEXP_M = 4` (include/mujs.h:82-84).

Engine semantics derived from the source, used to pick the expected results below:

* `js_regexec` returns `0` = match, `1` = no match, `-1` = recursion limit hit
  (regexp.c:1080-1081, 1222, 1075-1076).
* Every compiled program is prefixed with `split / anynl / jump` (regexp.c:967-972) where
  `split->x = split+3` is tried *before* `split->y`, so the search is **leftmost** and the
  start position advances one *rune* at a time, crossing newlines (`I_ANYNL`, regexp.c:1115-1119).
* `I_SPLIT` recurses into `pc->x` first and returns on the first success (regexp.c:1085-1095):
  the engine is **leftmost-first (backtracking / Perl)**, *not* POSIX leftmost-longest.
* `REG_ICASE` acts at compile time on `I_CHAR` (regexp.c:792) and at run time on
  `I_CHAR` / `I_CCLASS` / `I_NCCLASS` / `I_REF` (regexp.c:1130, 1139, 1151, 1162).
* `REG_NEWLINE` affects **only** `I_BOL` / `I_EOL` (regexp.c:1179, 1191); there is no dotall
  option, `I_ANY` always rejects newlines (regexp.c:1123).
* `REG_NOTBOL` affects **only** `I_BOL` (regexp.c:1175).
* `eflags` are OR-ed into `prog->flags` at exec time (regexp.c:1239), so `REG_ICASE` and
  `REG_NEWLINE` are also *accepted* (with partial effect) as exec flags.
* Group 0 is the whole match, so a pattern may contain at most **15** capturing groups
  (`g->nsub` starts at 1, regexp.c:931; `die` at regexp.c:551-552).
* There are no octal escapes and no dotall/sticky/unicode flags; `^` and `$` are recognised
  only at `parserep` level (regexp.c:588-589) and therefore cannot be quantified.
